content.text: The abnormal trace shows travel-service's queryInfo taking about 2 s while its children (a 9 ms DB query and a 94 ms basic call) account for only about 100 ms. That gap is self time. Separately, travel2 is absent from traces even though its pod reports metrics, so I'll check travel2's pod name across traces and logs.

SELECT attr_k8s_pod_name pod, metric, round(avg(value),3) av, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name='ts-travel-service' AND (metric LIKE 'container.cpu%' OR metric LIKE 'jvm.gc%' OR metric LIKE 'jvm.memory%' OR metric LIKE 'jvm.thread%' OR metric LIKE 'container.memory.usage' OR metric LIKE 'k8s.pod.cpu%') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2

content.text: Travel-service's container CPU is low (about 2% of its limit), so this isn't CPU saturation. I'll compare travel-service's outgoing calls by callee between periods.

input.query: WITH s AS (SELECT 'abn' p, span_id, parent_span_id, service_name, span_name, trace_id, duration FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', span_id, parent_span_id, service_name, span_name, trace_id, duration FROM normal_traces) SELECT c.p, par.service_name caller, par.span_name caller_span, c.service_name callee, c.span_name callee_span, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) ms FROM s c JOIN s par ON c.parent_span_id=par.span_id AND c.trace_id=par.trace_id AND c.p=par.p WHERE par.service_name='ts-travel-service' AND c.service_name<>par.service_name GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 3,4,1

content.text: Hubble shows travel2's pod still receiving connections in the abnormal period, with its callers' flows increasing (retries), while its spans and JVM metrics vanish. That points to the travel2 process being down behind a live pod. One more check: whether travel-service's queryInfo self time is explained by any child, in both periods.

input.query: WITH s AS (SELECT 'abn' p, span_id, parent_span_id, service_name, span_name, trace_id, duration FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', span_id, parent_span_id, service_name, span_name, trace_id, duration FROM normal_traces), q AS (SELECT p, trace_id, span_id, duration FROM s WHERE service_name='ts-travel-service' AND span_name='TravelController.queryInfo') SELECT q.p, count(*) n, round(avg(q.duration)/1e6,1) queryinfo_ms, round(avg(ch.kids)/1e6,1) children_ms, round(avg(q.duration - coalesce(ch.kids,0))/1e6,1) self_ms FROM q LEFT JOIN (SELECT p, parent_span_id, trace_id, sum(duration) kids FROM s GROUP BY 1,2,3) ch ON ch.parent_span_id=q.span_id AND ch.trace_id=q.trace_id AND ch.p=q.p GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: Aggregated, queryInfo's children explain most of its time (696 of 781 ms), so the earlier 2 s gap was a single outlier. I'll see which children carry that time.
